metadata.title: Database Security Hardening and Access Control

procedures.description: Audit current database user accounts and permissions
procedures.command: SELECT usename, usesuper, usecreatedb, usebypassrls FROM pg_user;
procedures.expected_result: List of all database users with their privilege levels

procedures.description: Enable SSL encryption for database connections
procedures.command: ALTER SYSTEM SET ssl = 'on'; SELECT pg_reload_conf();
procedures.expected_result: SSL encryption enabled for all database connections

procedures.command: ALTER TABLE sensitive_data ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
procedures.expected_result: Row-level security enabled for sensitive tables

procedures.command: ALTER SYSTEM SET log_statement = 'all'; SELECT pg_reload_conf();
procedures.expected_result: All database statements are logged for audit purposes

troubleshooting_steps.resolution: Verify SSL certificates, check pg_hba.conf settings, validate network connectivity
Optimize logging levels, improve log storage performance, implement proper log rotation

troubleshooting_steps.symptom: Access denied errors for legitimate users
troubleshooting_steps.resolution: Review security policies, verify role assignments, check permission inheritance

raw_content:
# Database Security Hardening

Essential procedures for implementing comprehensive database security measures and access controls.

## Security Layers
- Network security (firewalls, VPNs)
- Authentication and authorization
- Data encryption (at rest and in transit)
- Audit logging and monitoring
- Row-level and column-level security

## Compliance Requirements
- GDPR data protection
- SOC 2 security controls
- PCI DSS compliance
- Industry-specific regulations

## Security Best Practices
- Principle of least privilege
- Regular security audits
- Automated vulnerability scanning
- Incident response procedures
